title: Pricing & Billing Request Triage Runbook for Enterprise Customers
creator: Aarti Singh
description: Problem: Enterprise prospects and existing customers are sending varied requests related to commitments, invoicing formats, marketplace transactions, and cost allocation. There is no single authoritative triage path which leads to inconsistent prioritization, delayed responses, and missed contractual terms. Goal: Create a repeatable triage runbook that intake teams (AE, CSM, Sales Ops, PM) can follow to classify requests, identify required stakeholders (billing ops, legal, finance, engineering), and surface clear prioritization to product management. Scope: Non-bug requests only (pricing, packaging, invoicing, committed usage, cost allocation, marketplace SKU mapping). Out of scope: technical incidents, feature bugs, and ad-hoc account-level refunds (handled by support/finance workflow).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A single triage form/template exists and is documented for AE/CSM use with required fields: customer size, ARR, urgency, exact ask, contract references, desired billing cadence, marketplace involvement, and revenue recognition concerns.
A2: Triage decision matrix defined that maps request types to owners (Billing Ops, Finance, Legal, PM, Eng) and SLA targets (48h/5 business days/30 days).

A3: Prioritization rubric that balances customer ARR, legal/regulatory risk, product strategy fit, and implementation effort is documented and applied to three historical sample requests with recorded outcomes.
A4: An onboarding slide and short walkthrough recorded for Sales/CSM teams; at least 6 AEs/CSMs reviewed and signed off on the runbook during the cycle.
A5: A dashboard (Looker/Grafana) tracking incoming triage items by type, SLA, and decision outcome is live and populated with test data.
A6: A template response and routing email exists for common outcomes (Approve, Requires Contract Amend, Needs Engineering, Decline) and is approved by Legal and Finance.

proposed_solution: Deliver a three-part artifact set: (1) a canonical triage intake form (Google Form + Confluence template) with required metadata, (2) a decision matrix and prioritization rubric (Confluence doc) that maps to routing rules and SLAs, (3) a lightweight dashboard to track throughput and outcomes. Implementation: Sales Ops builds the form, PM authors the rubric, Billing Ops + Finance review templates, Eng evaluates any API changes required for invoicing or marketplace SKU mapping (ENG-2841).
tradeoffs: Fast templated intake reduces friction but may miss nuance for complex enterprise deals — mitigated by an 'escalate to PM' path in the flow.
Automating routing to Billing Ops can speed handling but requires upfront engineering work to integrate with CRM — delays initial rollout by ~2 sprints.
Tight SLAs prioritize revenue-impacting requests but may overload small Billing Ops team — recommend capacity plan and on-call rota.
